name: Blood Orange
label: RCA / Domino
lede: He screamed in Test Icicles at 18, wrote folk as Lightspeed Champion, then spent fifteen years as Blood Orange writing for Solange, Carly Rae Jepsen and Blondie before Pitchfork put his grief record at No. 24 of 2025.

eras.title: Two years of screaming in Ilford's shadow
eras.text: Dev Hynes was 18 when he joined a London trio that took dance-punk at the speed of a fire alarm. It lasted about as long as a school term and left him a stage name to shed.

years.h: [[Test Icicles|f1ce0a98-fed9-4337-b817-398720ff6bd8]]: Hynes joins Rory Attwell and Sam Mehran
years.p: The trio, all 18, met through London's club scene, including the Afterskool night. Dev Hynes played guitar, synth and the odd vocal.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Attwell and Mehran had been playing as Balls with Ferry Gouw before Hynes came in and the band took the Test Icicles name. Wikipedia lists the sound as dance-punk crossed with post-hardcore, played through Peavey and Fender amps.

years.h: For Screening Purposes Only, the only Test Icicles album
years.p: Released October 31, 2005. The singles "Circle. Square. Triangle" and "What's Your Damage" both cracked the UK top 40, at Nos. 25 and 31, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts the album at No. 69 in the UK. It was the band's whole studio catalogue.

years.h: Test Icicles split, then hand out a farewell EP
years.p: The band announced its breakup in February 2006. The remix-and-videos EP Dig Your Own Grave followed on April 26.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes Mehran later moved to New York and worked in music, and died in July 2018. It gives no cause. Attwell kept releasing music under other names.

eras.title: Lightspeed Champion: the cardigan years
eras.text: Hynes swapped screaming for songs, took a kid's comic-book alter ego on the road, and blew out his throat doing it.

years.cap: Dev Hynes as Lightspeed Champion at the Barfly, Cambridge · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Lightspeed Champion · Wikipedia: Falling Off the Lavender Bridge
years.h: Omaha: Hynes cuts a folk-rock debut with Mike Mogis
years.p: He flew to Nebraska to record with Saddle Creek producer [[Mike Mogis|0306016b-331c-4519-b51e-f11dfc217455]] at ARC Studios, backed by locals including Faint drummer Clark Baechle and Emmy the Great.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the name Lightspeed Champion came from comic strips Hynes drew in his school maths textbooks as a teenager. Trumpeter Nate Walcott and members of Cursive and Tilly and the Wall also played on the record.

years.h: "Galaxy of the Lost" is the first Lightspeed Champion single
years.p: It set up the album six months out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Falling Off the Lavender Bridge
years.h: Falling Off the Lavender Bridge on Domino
years.p: The title comes from a lavender toy frog his mother gave him as a child to help him sleep. It reached No. 45 on the UK albums chart.
years.xp: Hynes described the record as a mixture of his dreams and life experiences, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork gave it 6.3 and NME 9 out of 10, so the reviews were nothing like unanimous.

years.h: Florence Welch and friends fill out the touring band
years.p: [[Florence Welch|88798869-338b-418e-9c47-97365444b734]] and [[Emmy the Great|60bbceb2-0ddc-403b-970b-b4e9c3b2de5c]] played in the live band, with Alex Turner and Faris Badwan among the guests, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lightspeed Champion · Wikipedia: Coastal Grooves
years.h: Throat surgery ends the touring; Lightspeed Champion goes quiet
years.p: Wikipedia says two years of touring left Hynes with serious throat damage and he had extensive surgery. He was off the road for about two and a half years.
years.xp: The second album, Life Is Sweet! Nice to Meet You, came out in 2010 and the project then paused. Wikipedia's Coastal Grooves page ties his falsetto on the next record to the surgery.

eras.title: Blood Orange, from Brooklyn to Solange
eras.text: Hynes settled in New York, went by a new name and turned to R&B, synths and 1980s downtown glamour. He also began writing for other people.

years.h: First Blood Orange shows: a guitar and a laptop
years.p: Hynes played the first sets in New York and London in November and December 2009, per Wikipedia. He had lived in New York since 2007.

years.h: "Dinner" comes out on Terrible Records
years.p: The first Blood Orange single, released on the label Solange would also join.

years.h: Coastal Grooves, produced by Ariel Rechtshaid in Los Angeles
years.p: Domino sold it as New York in the 1980s. Pitchfork gave it 5.9, Metacritic averages 72.
years.xp: "Champagne Coast" went viral on TikTok in July 2024, thirteen years on, and reached No. 15 on Billboard's Hot Alternative Songs chart, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dev Hynes · Wikipedia: Solange Knowles
years.h: He co-writes and co-produces [[Solange Knowles|410e7fd3-b865-4fa0-bb18-1b7fd53382ca]]'s True EP
years.p: The EP was Solange's first for Terrible Records and reached iTunes on November 27, 2012.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Hynes as co-writer and co-producer of True. The same year he wrote "Everything Is Embarrassing" for [[Sky Ferreira|05f3353e-e2d9-4344-a3c9-8009dd8e0427]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Cupid Deluxe · Wikipedia: Lightspeed Champion
years.h: Cupid Deluxe makes Blood Orange a name
years.p: The 11-track album was written after moving from Brooklyn to Manhattan and features Caroline Polachek, David Longstreth, Skepta and Clams Casino.
years.xp: Hynes called it a record about life transitions, going from a stable position to an unstable one. Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and later placed it No. 35 on its top 200 albums of the 2010s. The Fader put him on the cover of issue 89 that month.

years.h: He scores Gia Coppola's Palo Alto
years.p: Hynes's first film score, and the start of a second career in soundtracks.

eras.title: Freetown Sound, Negro Swan and a hit for Carly Rae
eras.text: Hynes made two of the decade's most argued-over records about being Black and queer in the West, while writing pop for other people.

years.h: Hynes co-writes "All That" and "Body Language" for Carly Rae Jepsen
years.p: Both went on [[Carly Rae Jepsen|09887aa7-226e-4ecc-9a0c-02d2ae5777e1]]'s Emotion era, with "All That" co-produced too.

years.h: Freetown Sound: 17 songs named for his father's birthplace
years.p: Freetown, Sierra Leone. It samples writer Ta-Nehisi Coates and slam poet Ashlee Haze, and Pitchfork gave it 8.8.
years.xp: Guests include Carly Rae Jepsen, Nelly Furtado, Debbie Harry, Kelsey Lu and Empress Of. Wikipedia says it was shortlisted for IMPALA's 2016 Album of the Year and peaked at No. 159 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: He writes "Long Time" with Deborah Harry for Blondie
years.p: On Pollinator; it reached No. 5 on Billboard's Hot Dance chart.

years.h: Negro Swan: his own account of black depression
years.p: Hynes described the album as an honest look at the corners of black existence and the anxieties of queer people of color. Puff Daddy, A$AP Rocky and Steve Lacy guest.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.6 and ranked it No. 46 of 2018. Metacritic scored it 84.

years.h: He scores Queen & Slim and makes Fields with Third Coast Percussion
years.p: Fields was nominated for a Grammy for Best Chamber Music/Small Ensemble Performance.

eras.title: Scores, Glass and a TikTok afterlife
eras.text: Hynes scored films and a Broadway play and played Philip Glass at Carnegie Hall, before his own 2011 song found a new audience.

years.h: Soundtrack run: We Are Who We Are, Mainstream, Passing, Master Gardener
years.p: Wikipedia lists all four, plus performances of Philip Glass's piano Etudes at Carnegie Hall and the Kennedy Center.

years.h: Hynes signs to RCA
years.p: He then released the Four Songs EP in 2022 and played The Tonight Show.

years.h: He writes music for the Broadway play Job
years.p: A Broadway credit to go with the film scores.

years.h: "Champagne Coast" blows up on TikTok
years.p: The 2011 song from Coastal Grooves climbed to No. 15 on Hot Alternative Songs.

eras.title: Essex Honey
eras.text: A record about grief and the Essex he came from, with Lorde, Caroline Polachek and Zadie Smith on it.

years.h: "The Field" arrives with Caroline Polachek and Daniel Caesar
years.p: It features the Durutti Column too.

years.h: Hynes produces the Charlatans' We Are Love
years.p: Wikipedia credits him with producing the Charlatans' 2025 album.

years.h: Essex Honey: Pitchfork gives it 8.1 and No. 24 of 2025
years.p: RCA and Domino released it, self-produced. Metacritic averages 88; NME, the Guardian and Rolling Stone gave five stars.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Hynes made it amid a period of collective grief and loss, drawing on Elliott Smith and the Replacements. Guests include Lorde, Caroline Polachek, Daniel Caesar, Mustafa the Poet, Brendan Yates of Turnstile, Ben Watt, Tirzah, Zadie Smith and Amandla Stenberg. "Countryside" was the last single, on August 27.

years.h: He opens for Lorde and Turnstile on the road
years.p: Hynes supported [[Lorde|8e494408-8620-4c6a-82c2-c2ca4a1e4f12]]'s Ultrasound World Tour and Turnstile's Never Enough Tour.
